annotation.title_clean: 无人驾驶航空器飞行管理暂行条例
annotation.title_en: Interim Regulations on the Flight Management of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
annotation.authors_or_issuer: State Council of the People's Republic of China; Central Military Commission
annotation.summary_en: China's State Council Decree No. 761 (31 May 2023, in force 1 January 2024) sets up a national regime for unmanned aircraft. It sorts drones into micro, light, small, medium, large and agricultural classes and defines controlled airspace. It also sets flight-approval procedures, airworthiness, registration, operator licensing, liability insurance and incident reporting, with administrative penalties for breaches.
key_provisions_or_claims: Drones are sorted into classes by weight, speed and altitude (micro, light, small, medium, large, agricultural), and the lighter classes must allow a human to take over control at any time.
Airspace above 120 m true height, plus restricted and sensitive areas, is controlled airspace; flight applications are due by 12:00 the day before, with faster procedures for emergency missions.
Medium and large drones need airworthiness approval; manufacturers must give each drone a unique product identification code; civil drones need real-name registration.
Operators must hold operator licences, operating certificates and liability insurance; agricultural drones up to 150 kg flown in suitable airspace are exempt from the operating certificate.
Operators must report flight safety problems within 24 hours after landing; illegal counter-drone equipment and surveying flights by foreign drones or operators carry penalties.
